Biharnagybajom Jewish Cemetery

Jewish Cemetery · Biharnagybajom, Hungary

Not demolished. Biharnagybajom's Jewish community, previously under Oradea's Chief Rabbinate, formally organized in 1826, growing to 60 families by 1848 and electing Rabbi Jakab Gottlieb (formerly of Huszt) as its first rabbi; Jicchok Eisig succeeded him for 20 years after 1860, followed by Samuel Jungreisz and Manó Szófer. Between 1910-1926 the community operated without a rabbi even as its yeshiva (founded 1848) and Talmud Torah (1916) continued growing, though authorities eventually forced the elementary school's closure. Strictly Orthodox, the community's registry area extended to Báránd, Sáp, Bihartorda, Nagyrabé, Bothanszeg, and Pancsháza; by 1929, 149 members (32 taxpayers) worked mainly in trade. Five community members died in WWI. By 1944, 98 Jews remained (20 taxpayers), maintaining a synagogue, rabbi's residence, mikveh, and shochet's apartment. This cemetery's only confirmed tombstone dates to 1877.
